hypotheses.binder: (hJc : ∀ r : K, J - algebraMap K F r ≠ 0)
hypotheses.justification: `hj₀` already implies `hJc`. Suppose `J - algebraMap K F r = 0` for some `r`. Then `J - algebraMap K F j₀ = algebraMap K F (r - j₀)`. If `r = j₀`, this is `0`, and `Place.ord_zero` (Def_AlgebraicCurve_DivisorClassGroup.lean:125, `ord` is `-log adicValuation`) gives `ord 0 = 0`. If `r ≠ j₀`, it is a nonzero constant, and `HasseOrdBody.ord_algebraMap` (same file, line 27) gives ord `0`. Both cases contradict `1 ≤ v.ord (J - algebraMap K F j₀)`. So the new proof first derives `hJc` from `hj₀` this way, then runs the existing proof unchanged. These hypotheses can be removed independently of one another; all three can also be removed together, using the Taylor argument given under `[IsAlgClosed K]`.

`hev` forces `Q ≠ 0`. With `IsAlgClosed`, `Splits.eq_prod_roots` gives `Q = C Q.leadingCoeff * ∏ (X - C r)`. So `aeval J Q = algebraMap K F Q.leadingCoeff * ∏ (J - algebraMap r)`. Apply `v.ord_mul`: both factors are nonzero, since the leading coefficient is nonzero and each `J - algebraMap r ≠ 0` by `hJc`. The constant factor has ord `0` by `ord_algebraMap`, and the product has ord `0` exactly as in the current proof. Use `mem_roots` with `Q ≠ 0` from `hev` in place of `hQ.ne_zero`. So the result stays `0` without monicity.

The statement holds over any field `K`, by a direct ultrametric argument. Taylor-expand `Q` at `j₀` (`Polynomial.taylor`): `aeval J Q = Q.eval j₀ + Σ_{i≥1} c_i (J - algebraMap j₀)^i` with `c_i ∈ K`. Let `w = v.adicValuation`. By `hj₀`, `w(J - j₀) < 1`. Each term with `i ≥ 1` has `w ≤ w(J - j₀)^i < 1`: constants have `w ≤ 1` by `algebraMap_mem'`, and zero terms are trivially below 1. So by `Valuation.map_sum_lt` (Mathlib RingTheory/Valuation/Basic.lean:194) the tail has `w < 1`. `algebraMap (Q.eval j₀)` is a nonzero constant with `w = 1` (ord 0 by `ord_algebraMap`, using `hev`). Hence `Valuation.map_add_eq_of_lt_left` gives `w(aeval J Q) = 1`, i.e. ord `0`. No splitting is needed.
